main_claim: 160,000+ Product Hunt launches: entry rose sharply after ChatGPT-3.5, disproportionately by solo founders, but teams still dominate the top of the quality distribution.
use: Empirical support for the supervisor's 'entry barriers fell' framing, with the nuance that quality leaders remain few.
notes: Not peer reviewed.

title: AI coding tools and digital entrepreneurship: The role of software expertise
main_claim: Studies how digital ventures respond to the diffusion of AI coding tools, measuring product-category exposure, and whether tools substitute for founders' software expertise.
use: Second piece of evidence on lower entry barriers in software.
notes: Title differs from the one in search snippets ('How founder expertise shapes...'): earlier version. Not peer reviewed.

title: The economics of builder saturation in digital markets
main_claim: Model: GenAI cuts production costs but attention is finite; with free entry, more builders dilute average returns ('Builder Saturation Effect').
use: Theoretical reason why lower entry barriers need not hurt incumbents with distribution and users (complementary assets).
notes: Not peer reviewed.

title: Pricing and competition for generative AI
main_claim: Game-theoretic model of how developers of GenAI software release and price models when one model serves many tasks and users judge outputs by satisfaction.
use: Only to document that AI pricing research is mostly analytical modeling, not SaaS practice.
notes: Not peer reviewed.

authors: Cavero, F. J., Alonso, J. C., & Ruiz-Cortés, A.
title: From static to intelligent: Evolving SaaS pricing with LLMs
main_claim: Proposes machine-readable 'intelligent pricing' models and an LLM pipeline that turns SaaS pricing pages into structured models for analysis.
use: Method idea: structured coding of pricing pages (plans, limits, add-ons, AI credits) at t0/t1/t2.
notes: Not peer reviewed; same group publishes SaaS pricing datasets [M].

title: Pricing AI software services: Reallocating value and risk
main_claim: For agentic software services: work splits into a 'thinking layer' and a 'making layer' with different unit economics; inference prices are not yet a stable market rate (per-token prices as a positioning bid); proposes cost-decomposition, hybrid and value-anchored pricing regimes.
use: Supports reading AI pricing as cost-driven and unstable (strategy 5) and the rival outcome/value-anchored option.
notes: About software services (agencies), not SaaS products. Not peer reviewed.

authors: Ning, Y., Shi, Z., & Tong, Y.
title: Value-based or one-time? Optimal pricing modes for generative AI services in e-commerce platforms
main_claim: Analytical model comparing value-based and one-time pricing of GenAI services on e-commerce platforms. Content inferred from title only.
use: Possible citation that value-based pricing of GenAI is studied analytically; read before use.

title: Machine customers
main_claim: Two-page practitioner column on machine customers. Content not read.
use: Only peer-indexed item found on 'machine customers'; pair with Gartner (Scheibenreif & Raskino) from the grey-literature agent.

authors: Cherep, M., Ma, C., Xu, A., Shaked, M., Maes, P., & Singh, N.
title: A framework for studying AI agent behavior: Evidence from consumer choice experiments
main_claim: LLM agents act as a new class of economic actors; in a simulated shopping environment their choices shift predictably with prices, ratings and nudges (strongly biased choosers).
use: Optional evidence that agents behave as 'customers' with their own choice biases.
notes: Not peer reviewed.

authors: Rezazadeh, A., Kohns, M., Bohnsack, R., António, N., & Rita, P.
title: Generative AI for growth hacking: How startups use generative AI in their growth strategies
main_claim: Study of how start-ups use GenAI in growth strategies. Content inferred from title only.
use: Possible support for the AI-native entrant (Gamma) growth logic; read before use.

title: Generative AI and creative industries: A systematic review on emerging trends and future research directions
main_claim: PRISMA review (2004-2024) of GenAI in the creative economy: focuses on authorship, augmented creativity and production paradigms.
use: Shows that creative-industry GenAI research addresses creators and work, not software vendors' business models.
notes: Lower-tier outlet.

authors: Li, Z., Liu, H., Shan, S., Zhang, M., & Yang, Q.
title: When AI hurts the pros: Expertise-fixation costs and platform deployment of generative AI in subscription markets
main_claim: Two-sided market model: whether subscription content platforms should deploy GenAI depends on a cost threshold and on heterogeneous effects on novice vs expert creators.
use: Optional: cost threshold logic for deploying GenAI in subscription platforms (cost-driven decisions).

authors: Gibbert, M., Ruigrok, W., & Wicki, B.
title: What passes as a rigorous case study?
main_claim: Analysis of case studies in 10 management journals (1995-2000): they emphasize external validity at the expense of internal and construct validity; identifies strategies for rigor.
use: Structure of the validity and limitations section (construct, internal, external validity, reliability).

authors: Garousi, V., Felderer, M., & Mäntylä, M. V.
title: Guidelines for including grey literature and conducting multivocal literature reviews in software engineering
main_claim: Guidelines for multivocal literature reviews: when and how to include grey literature, search, source selection, quality assessment of grey sources. [M] summary.
use: Justifies the systematic use of grey literature (Bain, IDC, pricing pages, developer docs) and a quality checklist for it.
